name: Rubellite
physical: Traditionally associated with warmth and vitality
Said to bring a sense of get-up-and-go
Crystal healers link it with a lively circulation of energy
summary: Rubellite is the deep raspberry-red tourmaline, a fiery heart stone linked in crystal lore with passion, courage, devotion and vitality.
intro: Rubellite is tourmaline in its richest red-to-pink colours, from raspberry and cherry to a purplish ruby tone. The stones are famous for their saturated colour that glows by daylight and lamp light alike. Gem-quality crystals are often heavily included, and slightly cloudy stones are treated as part of their charm, though eye-clean examples fetch high prices. Slender prisms from Brazil, Nigeria and Mozambique show lengthwise striations and a rounded triangular cross-section. Compared with softer pinks, rubellite feels bolder and more urgent, a stone with presence on the hand and on the shelf.
history: For centuries red tourmaline was confused with ruby and spinel, and some historic gemstones in European treasuries were later found to be rubellite. The Russian Tsars were particularly fond of the stone, and in the nineteenth century Russian buyers favoured rubellite from the Ural region. The Chinese imperial court also prized red and pink tourmaline from California in the 1800s, with the Dowager Empress purchasing many tons. The name comes from the Latin rubellus, meaning reddish. Modern sources include Brazil, Nigeria, Madagascar and Mozambique, and the gem is still mounted in fine jewelry as a hardier, more affordable alternative to ruby.
meaning: Rubellite is a stone of warm, active love and personal courage. Crystal practitioners say it combines the stability of the root chakra with the openness of the heart chakra, making it good for people who want to act on their feelings rather than merely hold them. It is traditionally used to rekindle enthusiasm in relationships, work and creative projects, and to bring a feeling of bold confidence when starting something new. Some healers recommend it during times of low motivation or when life feels grey. Its fiery colour is also tied to devotion and loyalty. Physically it is associated with vitality and warmth, a supportive companion for active days, though it is never used as a replacement for medical advice.
howToUse: Wear rubellite as a ring or pendant when you need a little extra boldness, such as on a date night, before a pitch or at the start of a new project. In meditation, hold the stone against the lower belly or chest and breathe slowly, imagining warm red light. Place a piece in the south of a room in feng shui practice to support passion and recognition. Pair it with citrine for motivation, or with rose quartz for loving energy. A small prism by your workout bag can serve as a talisman for energy.
care: Rubellite is hard and tolerates a rinse in lukewarm water, though included stones should avoid ultrasonic cleaners and sudden heat. Cleanse with smoke, sound or selenite. The colour can fade in prolonged, strong sunlight, so give it moonlight instead. Keep polished gems separate from harder stones such as sapphire and diamond, and wrap raw prisms in soft cloth since the long crystals can snap. Wipe jewelry with a soft cloth after wearing.
identify: Genuine rubellite shows a deep pinkish to purplish red, often with feathery inclusions and fine striations on raw crystals. It is dichroic, shifting slightly in tone as it is turned. Look-alikes include ruby, red spinel, garnet and red glass. Irradiation and heat are commonly used to improve colour, and a few stones are fracture-filled. Perfect, flawless stones at low prices should be suspected, and expensive pieces should have a lab report that confirms the species and treatments.

faq.a: Rubellite is the red to deep pink variety of tourmaline. It was once confused with ruby, but it is a different mineral and is generally softer on the budget, while still hard enough for jewelry.

In crystal tradition it stands for passionate love, courage and devotion. People use it to bring warmth to relationships and to feel bold about new projects, linking it with the root and heart chakras.

faq.q: Can rubellite be worn every day?
faq.a: Yes, with ordinary care. Its hardness of about 7 to 7.5 resists daily wear, though included stones can be brittle and rings should be protected from sharp knocks and strong sunlight over time.
